failure_modes: If the observed-teacher contrast is itself non-monotone within [0.0,0.5], a 0.5 blend can chase sign changes and displace surrounding coordinates unnecessarily; the landmark curves show 4-6 sign changes, so partial-blend overshoot is a concrete risk.

If pair-kernel contrast is a diagnostic coordinate contrast rather than a force the executed pointcloud scalar contains, the expected endpoint-affinity gain may not materialize; the executed scalar has no pair-kernel term, so the blend acts only through regional attention.

No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied (recorded affinities removed, equal score prior), so final-affinity benefit of C010 cannot be verified from these observations and could be null or negative.
A constant static rule could match the time-conditioned rule on observed-node fit fidelity (relative_node_RMSE), falsifying H002 and making the blend unnecessary displacement.
result.rationale: Analyst's strongest and most consistent endpoint-integrated contrasts are the pair-kernel coordinate contrasts (pair_kernel_2.5 z=0.63, 14/14 batches; pair_kernel_1.5 z=0.56, 14/14; pair_kernel_3.5 z=0.54, 14/14), while shape_yy/shape_xx are consistently negative (0/14 and 1/14 positive). H001 therefore points to a time-conditioned regional attention rule that upweights compact 1.5-3.5 A pair-kernel-consistent endpoint geometry and downweights yy/xx anisotropy. H002 is supported by the non-monotone landmark contrast curves (4-6 sign changes, first/last rate z of opposite sign, polynomial_accepted=false, extrapolation disallowed), which rules out a constant static rule and favors a time-conditioned blend using observed-node interpolation only. The registered temporal_teacher recipe (1-blend)*R_static + blend*R_observed_teacher(time) changes only regional attention at observed score nodes, keeps the same shared FLOWR endpoint and static teachers, and adds no velocity target, so it is the permitted time-conditioned alternative to the stationary coordinate target. C010 (temporal_teacher_blend=0.5) is chosen over C009 (0.25) and C011 (1.0): the observed window is short (50 score times, support [0.0,0.49]) and the contrast curves are non-monotone, so a full blend (C011) would over-trust a single observed-teacher trajectory and risk sign-flip overshoot, while 0.25 under-uses the validated temporal contrast; 0.5 balances the incumbent static rule against the observed-teacher signal. This is a dose/attention change only, not a teacher-coordinate or temperature change; fixed temperatures (mixture 0.5, teacher_endpoint 4.0) and teacher provenance are preserved. Affinity-first priority is respected because the edit targets the endpoint coordinate observable that carries the strongest signed endpoint-integrated contrast, and no decoded terminal affinity labels are available to justify a larger structural change.
